answers_by_date.basis: The regime was DL 1.094 (1975) and DS 597 (1984). Under DL 1.094, art. 14 only lets a minor with no parent or guardian stay in Chile in their entry residence status until age 18. Under DS 597, art. 27 No. 4 makes unaccompanied minors without authorisation a ground for refusing entry. Neither is a protection regime for migrant children, and no practice evidence for this period was read.

No change from 2000: DL 1.094 art. 14 and DS 597 were unchanged on this point. Executive measures on schooling and health access for children (circulars and agreements) are not decrees with force of law, and none was read. No practice evidence was read.
Still DL 1.094 and DS 597. Ley 20.430 (with its procedure for unaccompanied minors seeking asylum) was only published on 15 April 2010, so it was not yet in force. No practice evidence was read.

In force by now: Ley 20.430 arts. 38-40 (from 15 April 2010) and Decreto 837 arts. 54-57 (from 17 February 2011), which set a special procedure for asylum-seeking children. These remained unchanged through 1 January 2020, where the MRD answer is 'No', so no event separates 2015 from 2020 and the answer stays 'No' (see starting_answer_concern). No practice evidence was read.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been no right protections neither in 2000 nor in 2020

events.what_changed: Sets a special asylum procedure for minors. Every minor may apply for refugee status independently of their legal representative, and for unaccompanied or separated minors the child-protection authority must be notified and UNHCR guidelines followed. This reaches asylum-seeking children only.
events.passage: Artículo 39.- Menores no Acompañados o Separados. Cuando la solicitud fuese presentada por un menor de edad no acompañado o separado de su familia, la Secretaría Técnica de la Comisión de Reconocimiento informará, de inmediato, a la autoridad de menores, de manera que se ejerzan las medidas de protección, cuidado y asistencia que sean necesarias.

events.what_changed: Repeals the DL 1.094 rules on refugees. Ley 20.430 replaces them; the repealed DL 1.094 refugee articles were not read for child-specific content.
events.passage: Artículo 49.- Deróganse las normas establecidas en el decreto ley Nº1.094, de 1975, en lo que digan relación con los refugiados.

events.what_changed: Requires an age-sensitive interpretation of the refugee definition (art. 3). Defines separated, unaccompanied and orphaned children, requires immediate notice to the child-protection authority, and requires a child-rights expert at interviews of unaccompanied children (arts. 54-57). Asylum seekers only.
events.passage: Tratándose de menores de edad separados de su familia, no acompañados o huérfanos, la Secretaría Técnica deberá informar de inmediato a la autoridad de protección de derechos de niños, niñas o adolescentes para que se adopten las medidas de protección, cuidado y asistencia que se estimen necesarias.

events.passage: Artículo 33 bis.- Las víctimas del delito previsto en el artículo 411 quáter del Código Penal, que no sean nacionales o residentes permanentes en el país, tendrán derecho a presentar una solicitud de autorización de una residencia temporal por un período mínimo de seis meses

answers.starting_answer_concern: On 1 January 2020 national law already gave migrant children special treatment. Ley 20.430 arts. 38-40 and Decreto 837 arts. 3 and 54-57 (in force since 2010/2011) give asylum-seeking children an independent right to apply, immediate notice to the child-protection authority, a child-rights expert at interviews and age-sensitive interpretation. DL 1.094 art. 14 lets an unaccompanied minor remain until 18. A 'Yes' limited to asylum-seeking and unaccompanied children looks defensible for 2015 and 2020; the coder seems to have looked only at general migration law.
answers.notes: Answers are kept at 'No' for every date to match the starting answer, because no event between 2015 and 2020 separates them. If the starting answer were corrected to 'Yes', the change would date from 15 April 2010 (Ley 20.430) and 17 February 2011 (Decreto 837), giving 2015 'Yes' and 2000/2005/2010 'No'. No court ruling was relied on, and no treaty (the CRC) was treated as directly applicable. No practice sources were read, since implementation is 'Does Not Apply'.

answers_by_date.basis: DL 1.094 and DS 597 contain nothing protective for vulnerable migrant women. DL 1.094 art. 32 only treats a foreign woman married to a Chilean as a temporary resident. No practice evidence was read.
Unchanged from 2000. Administrative measures (e.g. on health care for pregnant migrants) are not law with force of law and none was read. No practice evidence was read.
Ley 20.430 was not yet published (15 April 2010), and Ley 20.507 on trafficking came in April 2011. No practice evidence was read.

In force by now: Ley 20.430 arts. 30 and 41 (same-sex interviewers; psychosocial assistance for asylum applicants who suffered sexual or gender-based violence), Decreto 837 arts. 3 and 58 (gender-sensitive interpretation), and DL 1.094 art. 33 bis (trafficking victims, not gender-specific). All were unchanged through 2020, where the MRD answers 'No', so the answer stays 'No' (see starting_answer_concern). No practice evidence was read.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been no right protections neither in 2000 nor in 2020
